Hongkong, 25th, Jan. 1923.

VERY SECRET

H. G. Simms, Esq.,
c/o Union Insurance Society of Canton, Ltd.
SHANGHAI.

My dear Simms,
Many thanks for your letter of the 10th instant
in re. the erection of a broadcasting station on the Dollar
Building in Shanghai. I can confirm that the "China Press"
are assisting in the enterprise. You know, of course, that
the "China Press" was purchased by the Sun Yat Sen interests.
All Sun Yat Sen's machinations in the South have been
directed against the British, and his anti-British propaganda
is wellknown.
My information was to the effect that in conjunction
with some Americans, the broadcasting station was to be used
in Shanghai by Sun to continue his anti-British propaganda in
the North. It is just conceivable, since the Doctor is now
apparently without funds, that he may try to make friends with
the British for the time being, but his tendencies are
wellknown. In this connection, I send you a photograph of a
letter written by Sun's secretary to one of the trade unions
here, which would clearly indicate what we suspected all
along that in the event of his returning to Canton, he would
foster, or try to foster a general strike. It appears from
information received that at the moment he hesitates to come
to Canton, although the Consul-General in Canton has been
applied to, to arrange for the "Wing Poong" to proceed to
Hongkong to bring up Sun. There is, therefore, a probability
that sooner or later, the Doctor will attempt a landing in
Canton. We are not in the least interested in the politics of
China, but both Hongkong & Shanghai are very much interested

香港，1923年1月25日。

绝密

H. G. Simms 先生，
转交广东联合保险有限公司，
上海。

亲爱的 Simms：
非常感谢你本月10日来信，关于在上海美元大楼（Dollar Building）设立广播电台一事。我可以证实，《字林西报》（China Press）正在协助此项事业。你当然知道，《字林西报》已被孙中山势力收购。孙中山在南方的一切阴谋活动均针对英国人，其反英宣传众所周知。
我所获情报显示，该广播电台将由孙中山与一些美国人合作，在上海用于继续在北方进行其反英宣传。鉴于孙博士目前显然缺乏资金，他暂时试图与英国人修好也是 conceivable（可设想）的，但其倾向性众所周知。就此而言，我随信附上孙中山秘书写给本地某工会的一封信的照片，这清楚地表明了我们一直以来的怀疑：即一旦他返回广州，他将煽动或试图煽动总罢工。据收到的情报显示，目前他犹豫是否前往广州，尽管已向驻广州总领事提出申请，安排“永丰”号（Wing Poong）前往香港接孙中山。因此，孙博士迟早会尝试在广州登陆的可能性是存在的。我们对中国政治毫无兴趣，但香港和上海都非常关心

pages.en:
in the strike question, and I therefore give you this
information which can be used among the British Members
of the Council if thought by yourself desirable.

Yours sincerely,

ENCLOSURE
Hartague Ede.

Translation of Photograph of Letter.
------------------

To the Managers of Labour Organizations in
Canton, Hongkong and Macao, o/o Dear Siang Jung(湘芹 ),

When the traitor raised the standard
of rebellion, I, Vung (one of Dr. Sun Yat Sen's
pseudonyms) had to take refuge in Shanghai.
Since then the traitor, Chen(陳 ) has been
unrelenting in his efforts to destroy the
accomplishments of my Constitutional policy and
has oppressed labour. The officials of Hongkong
and Macao, actuated by the same aims, dissolved
labour organizations for trifling reasons.
According to statements of representatives of
labour unions who have come to Shanghai, cases
in which the traitor and the officials of
Hongkong and Macao cruelly illtreated the
labourers are so numerous that they cannot be
counted. The request of the labour organiza-
tions that I, Vung, support a general strike
which they intend to declare, deserves sympathy.
However the time is not opportune for such
action. The rebels still occupy the city of
Canton, and consequently promoters of a strike
there at the present time would be running a
very great risk. The Righteous armies from the
East and West will soon advance together to
attack traitor Chen and the rebels will soon
be obliged to forfeit their lives. As their
hour of reckoning is drawing near, I hope you
will be patient. As regards the request of
the representatives to open the Huang Poo
Kong(黃埔港) Harbour and to abolish the
present harbour, I have been considering this
idea for a long time, I have now sent Mr. Liao
(廖 ) to the South to take charge of affairs
there. I shall do my best to give every
possible assistance when I return to the South.

Stamp of the Secretariat.
18th.

致广州、香港和澳门劳工组织负责人，o/o 亲爱的湘芹 (Siang Jung)，

当叛贼举起反旗时，我，Vung（孙逸仙博士的化名之一），不得不避难于上海。此后，叛贼陈 (Chen) 不遗余力地破坏我宪政政策的成果，并压迫劳工。香港和澳门的官员出于同样的目的，以琐碎的理由解散劳工组织。根据前来上海的工会代表的陈述，叛贼以及香港和澳门官员残酷虐待工人的案例数不胜数。劳工组织请求我，Vung，支持他们打算宣布的总罢工，这值得同情。然而，此时采取此类行动的时机并不成熟。叛军仍占据广州城，因此目前在那裡鼓动罢工的人将面临极大的风险。来自东西方的正义之师很快将联合进攻叛贼陈，叛军不久将被迫送命。由于他们的清算时刻临近，我希望你们保持耐心。至于代表们提出的开放黄埔港 (Huang Poo Kong) 并废除现有港口的请求，我已考虑此想法良久，现已派遣廖先生 (Mr. Liao) 前往南方负责当地事务。当我回到南方时，我将尽力提供一切可能的协助。

秘书处印章。
18日。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JANUARY 27, 1923

DR. SUN YAT-SEN
CONGRATULATES
CHINA PRESS RADIO

Southern Leader Delighted
With Innovation—Predicts
Great Educational Value

Dr. Sun Yat-sen, on the eve of
his departure for Canton, to re-
sume the active leadership of the
Constitutionalist cause, yesterday
congratulated THE CHINA PRESS
and the Radio Corporation of
China on the introduction of the
radio to China and expressed his
utmost confidence that it would
prove a success in every way and
would greatly assist in spreading
the light in China.

“I was especially gratified
that my manifesto, which was
made public in THE CHINA PRESS
this morning, should have been
broadcasted from THE CHINA
PRESS station on top of the Dollar
building,” Dr. Sun said.

“It was my earnest hope that
every one in China should read or
hear my manifesto and the fact
that it was broadcasted and heard
by hundreds of people with receiv-
ing sets—some of them as far
away as Tientsin and Hongkong
—is a delightful surprise and a
great pleasure. We who are
working for the reunification of
this great country of ours wel-
come such forward steps as the
radio. It will not only closely
link China orally with the rest of
the world, but it will greatly
assist in knitting the various
cities and provinces of the coun-
try much more closely together.”

Dr. Sun’s manifesto, together
with the information that he was
leaving for Canton on Saturday—
news that a large portion of
China has been awaiting to hear
—was broadcasted from The
CHINA PRESS-Radio Corporation
of China broadcasting station on
Thursday night with other news,
bulletins from China and other
parts of the world. News is
broadcasted every night.

《字林西报》，1923年1月27日，星期六

孙逸仙博士
祝贺
《字林西报》电台

南方领袖对创新感到高兴——预测其具有巨大的教育价值

孙逸仙博士在启程前往广州、重新积极领导护法运动的前夕，昨日祝贺《字林西报》和中国无线电公司（Radio Corporation of China）将无线电引入中国，并表示他完全相信无线电将在各方面取得成功，并将极大地有助于在中国传播光明。

“令我特别欣慰的是，我的宣言今早在《字林西报》公开发表后，竟能从美元大楼顶部的《字林西报》电台广播出去，”孙博士说。

“我衷心希望中国的每个人都能读到或听到我的宣言，而事实上，它被广播并被数百名拥有接收器的人听到——其中一些人远在天津和香港——这是一个令人愉快的惊喜和巨大的快乐。我们这些致力于这个伟大国家统一的人，欢迎像无线电这样的进步举措。它不仅将通过声音使中国与世界各地紧密联系，还将极大地有助于将国内各城市和各省份更紧密地联结在一起。”

孙博士的宣言，连同他将于周六启程前往广州的消息——这是中国大部分地区一直等待听到的新闻——于周四晚间与其他新闻、来自中国及世界其他地方的简报一起，从《字林西报》-中国无线电公司广播电台播出。新闻每晚播出。

CENTRAL Station.
January 9 1923

REPORT ON Plans for the Erection of Broadcasting Station
in Shanghai.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

Enquiries made regarding attached confirm the
information that Mr. E. G. Osborne, who is manager of the
Radio Corporation of China, is making arrangements with
Harold Dollar for the erection of a broadcasting station on
the Dollar Building in Shanghai, and there is reason to
believe that the owners and employees of the China Press
are assisting the enterprise. No corroboration can however
be obtained of the statement that the station will be used
by Dr. Sun Yat Sen for the diffusion of anti-British propaganda.
E. G. Osborne is living in the Astor House. The directors
of the China Press consist of: Messrs Hugo Reiss, Stirling
Fessenden, Chu Pao San, Harold Dollar, Cheng Nieh Yun and
C. L. Seitz. Both Chu Pao San and Cheng Nieh Yun are
probably pro-British.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I. Givens
D. I.

D. C. I.

关于在上海设立广播电台计划的报告。

由 D. I. Givens 制作，经刑事侦缉处处长转发。

先生，

经查询所附事项，证实了以下信息：中国无线电公司经理 E. G. Osborne 先生正与 Harold Dollar 安排在上海美元大楼设立广播电台，且有理由相信《字林西报》的所有者和员工正在协助此项事业。然而，对于该电台将被孙逸仙博士用于散布反英宣传的说法，无法获得佐证。
E. G. Osborne 住在礼查饭店（Astor House）。《字林西报》的董事包括：Hugo Reiss 先生、Stirling Fessenden 先生、朱葆三 (Chu Pao San) 先生、Harold Dollar 先生、程聂云 (Cheng Nieh Yun) 先生和 C. L. Seitz 先生。朱葆三和程聂云两人可能都亲英。

我是，先生，
您顺从的仆人，
D. I. Givens
侦探督察 (D. I.)

刑事侦缉处处长 (D. C. I.)

UNION INSURANCE SOCIETY OF CANTON, LTD
INCORPORATED IN HONGKONG.
HEAD OFFICE,
HONGKONG.
ESTABLISHED 1835.
TELEGRAPHIC ADDRESS
"UNION, HONGKONG".
ALL COMMUNICATIONS TO BE ADDRESSED
TO THE GENERAL MANAGER.
HONGKONG, 28th Dec. 1922.
PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL
H. G. Simms, Esq.
c/o Union Insurance Society of Canton, Ltd.
S H A N G H A I.
My dear Simms,
It has come to my notice through a
Mr. W.V.Curtis here that a man of the name of Osborn
of Shanghai, an electrical engineer, is in treaty with
Harold Dollar to erect a broadcasting station on the
Dollar Building in Shanghai. Harold Dollar, as you know,
is mixed up with Hugo Reiss and one named Seitz, and
they are in turn mixed up with the "China Press" and
Sun Yat-sen; the object of the erection of this station
is, I understand, to enable Sun Yat-sen to broadcast
propaganda which may be relied upon to be anti-British.
I thought this information would be useful
to you, and therefore pass it on. You can, no doubt,
through your myrmidons, obtain the information as
required.
Yours sincerely,
Montagu S.
